ev-bar-kokhba-revolt:coord.reason: Ours marks Betar (Battir), the revolt's last stronghold per Cassius Dio and Eusebius; Wikidata's 32.5,34.9 is a generic point on the coastal plain. Note added.

ev-byzantine-sasanian-war-602:coord.reason: Plotted at Nineveh, site of Heraclius' decisive victory in December 627 (noted in record); Wikidata's 33.7,43.5 is an arbitrary central-Iraq point.
checked: J. Howard-Johnston, The Last Great War of Antiquity (2021)

ev-early-muslim-conquests:year.reason: Expansion beyond Arabia begins after Muhammad's death in 632 (Ridda wars, 633 Iraq campaign); Wikidata's 622 folds in Muhammad's own Arabian campaigns. Kennedy and Britannica start the conquests in 632/633.
checked: H. Kennedy, The Great Arab Conquests (2007)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Islamic world – the conquests

ev-battle-of-nahavand:coord.reason: Wikidata's 31.583,44.5 duplicates the al-Qadisiyyah coordinate in Iraq. Nahavand lies in the Zagros at c. 34.19 N, 48.37 E, where the curated point sits.

ev-abbasid-revolution:coord.reason: Movement spanned Khorasan to Iraq; curated point is Kufa, where al-Saffah was proclaimed caliph (749); the route starts near Merv (June 747, Iranica). Wikidata's 36,62 is a vague Khorasan point. Note added.
checked: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Abū Moslem (https://www.iranicaonline.org/?p=47484) – declaration Ramaḍān/Šawwāl 129 = June 747 near Merv

ev-shahnameh:year.reason: Iranica (Ferdowsi, i. Life) dates the completed second redaction to 25 Esfand 378 Š. / 400 AH = 8 March 1010; c. 1000 on Wikidata is a vague floruit. A first version was finished in 384/994.
checked: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Ferdowsi, Abu'l-Qāsem i. Life (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/ferdowsi-i)
Review of A. Khatibi in Al-ʿUṣūr al-Wusṭā (Columbia)

ev-first-crusade-levant:coord.reason: Record renamed from ev-first-crusade (id collided with data/europe). Point at Antioch, the crusade's longest siege (1097–98), is defensible; Wikidata's 34,36 is a generic Levant point. Old key not used, to avoid resolving the Europe record's diff.
checked: T. Asbridge, The First Crusade: A New History (2004)

ev-ottoman-mamluk-war:coord.reason: Point is Marj Dabiq (Dabiq village, c. 36.53 N 37.27 E), the decisive battle of 24 August 1516; Wikidata's 39,35 is a central-Anatolia centroid.
checked: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ottoman Empire – Selim I

ev-isfahan-capital:year.reason: Wikidata's 1591 is the inception of Naqsh-e Jahan Square (the linked item), not the transfer. Iranica: most scholars date the move from Qazvin to Isfahan to 1006/1598, though it was gradual.
checked: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Isfahan vii. Safavid period (https://iranicaonline.org/articles/isfahan-vii-safavid-period)
De Gruyter/Edinburgh UP chronology: 1598 official transfer of capital to Isfahan (https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/9780748633760-007/pdf)

ev-treaty-of-turkmenchay:coord.reason: Treaty was signed at the village of Torkamanchay (c. 37.60 N, 47.39 E) in East Azerbaijan; Wikidata's coordinate is Tabriz, ~110 km away.
checked: APA: city which hosted Turkmenchay treaty (https://en.apa.az/south-azerbaijan/city-which-hosted-turkmenchay-treaty-research-416201)

ev-persian-constitutional-revolution:coo.reason: The bast protests, the Majles and the 1906 constitution were centred in Tehran; Wikidata's 32,53 is Iran's centroid.
checked: E. Abrahamian, Iran Between Two Revolutions (1982)

ev-young-turk-revolution:coord.reason: The CUP was headquartered in Salonica and the July 1908 revolt began in Ottoman Macedonia (Resne, Monastir); Wikidata's 41,29 is a generic Istanbul-area point. Symbolic placement noted in record.
checked: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Young Turk Revolution of 1908

ev-armenian-genocide:coord.reason: Deir ez-Zor was the terminus of the deportation routes and the site of the largest massacres of 1916; Wikidata's 41,29 (Istanbul area) marks only the 24 April arrests. Symbolic placement noted.
checked: R. G. Suny, They Can Live in the Desert but Nowhere Else (2015)

ev-arab-revolt:year.reason: The revolt was proclaimed at Mecca on 10 June 1916 and ended with the entry into Damascus in October 1918; Wikidata's start-type value 1918 conflicts with its own 1916 start.
checked: E. Rogan, The Fall of the Ottomans (2015)

ev-saudi-arabia-1932:year.reason: The Wikidata item is the 1902–1932 unification process; the event plotted is the royal decree proclaiming the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, effective 23 September 1932 (National Day).
checked: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Saudi Arabia – the kingdom of Saudi Arabia
M. al-Rasheed, A History of Saudi Arabia (2010)

ev-saudi-arabia-1932:coord.reason: Riyadh was Ibn Saud's capital and seat of the proclamation; Wikidata's 23,46 is a generic central-Arabia point.
checked: M. al-Rasheed, A History of Saudi Arabia (2010)

ev-iranian-revolution:coord.reason: The decisive demonstrations, Khomeini's return and the February 1979 collapse of the monarchy took place in Tehran; Wikidata gives Iran's centroid.
checked: E. Abrahamian, A History of Modern Iran (2008)

ev-iran-iraq-war:coord.reason: Khorramshahr on the Shatt al-Arab was the war's emblematic front (taken 1980, retaken 1982); Wikidata gives Iran's centroid, far from the fighting.

ev-iraq-war:coord.reason: Baghdad, whose fall on 9 April 2003 ended Saddam's government, is a better anchor than Wikidata's 33,43 desert point west of the capital.

polity-arsacid-armenia:from.reason: 12 CE (Vonones I, Wikipedia) vs. 52/53–66 for Tiridates I; Iranica says he was recognised in 63, crowned by Nero in 66, and no stable line formed until Vologases II. Record medium, note updated.
checked: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Arsacids vii. The Arsacid dynasty of Armenia (https://iranicaonline.org/articles/arsacids-vii)
World History Encyclopedia: Arsacid Dynasty of Armenia (https://www.worldhistory.org/Arsacid_Dynasty_of_Armenia/)

polity-kingdom-of-georgia:to.reason: 1466 marks Bagrat VI's seizure of Imereti during the civil war; the unified kingdom ended with the formal partition of 1490–91, when Constantine II recognised Kakheti and Imereti. Record already medium with note.
checked: D. Rayfield, Edge of Empires: A History of Georgia (2012)
Wikipedia: Collapse of the Georgian realm; Constantine II of Georgia (recognition of Kakheti and Imereti, 1490–91)

polity-saudi-arabia:from.reason: Wikidata's 1727 is the founding of the Emirate of Diriyah (first Saudi state); this record is the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, proclaimed 1932.
checked: M. al-Rasheed, A History of Saudi Arabia (2010)

ev-nizamiyya-baghdad:year.reason: The college was founded in 457 AH/1065 and inaugurated in Dhu al-Qa'da 459 AH/September 1067 (Makdisi; Britannica 'Nizamiyyah' gives 1067). The record marks the opening; Wikidata's 1065 is the founding. Note added.

ev-hejaz-railway:coord.reason: Wikidata's point (32.63, 36.10) is near Daraa on the northern section. The event is the line reaching Medina, its terminus, formally opened on 1 September 1908 (Otago Witness, 21 Oct 1908; The Spectator, 5 Sep 1908).

ev-trajan-parthian-campaign:coord.reason: Plotted at Ctesiphon, the Parthian capital Trajan took in 116 (route carries the other stops); Wikidata 34,36 is a generic Syria point near Homs, outside the theatre of operations.

ev-julian-persian-expedition:coord.reason: Plotted at Ctesiphon, where Julian fought his main battle in 363; Wikidata 33.7,43.5 is an undefined point in the Anbar desert. Route records Antioch, Carrhae and the retreat.

ev-marib-dam-collapse:year.reason: Q2303666 covers the Marib dam site; its inception 1986 is the modern replacement dam. This record is the final breach of the ancient Sabaean dam in the late 6th century (low confidence, note).

ev-ridda-wars:coord.reason: Plotted at al-Yamama (Aqraba), site of the decisive battle against Musaylima in 632/633; Wikidata 23,46 is a centroid of Arabia.
checked: E. Shoufani, Al-Riddah and the Muslim Conquest of Arabia (1973)

ev-babak-revolt:coord.reason: Plotted at Babak Fort (Badhdh) near Kaleybar, the rebels’ stronghold taken by Afshin in 837; Wikidata 37.6,47 is a generic Azerbaijan point.

ev-zanj-rebellion:coord.reason: Plotted at Basra, centre of the salt-flat labour and sacked by the Zanj in 871; Wikidata 31.32,48.68 is Ahvaz, which the rebels also took but which was peripheral.
checked: A. Popovic, The Revolt of African Slaves in Iraq (1999)

ev-ottoman-capture-of-bursa:year.reason: Wikidata gives the start of the blockade (1317); the city surrendered to Orhan on 2 Jumada I 726 AH = 6 April 1326, the date this record marks.
checked: Turkish Ministry of Culture, Bursa: The First Capital City of the Ottoman Empire (https://bursa.ktb.gov.tr/EN-91280/the-first-capital-city-of-the-ottoman-empire.html)
H. İnalcık, The Ottoman Empire: The Classical Age (1973)

ev-celali-revolts:year.reason: Wikidata spans all Celali risings (1519–1659). This record is explicitly the great wave of c. 1595–1610 (Griswold; White), suppressed by Kuyucu Murad Pasha; note explains.
checked: W. J. Griswold, The Great Anatolian Rebellion 1591–1611 (1983)
S. White, The Climate of Rebellion in the Early Modern Ottoman Empire (2011)

ev-celali-revolts:endYear.reason: See :year. The great revolts end with Kuyucu Murad Pasha’s campaigns of 1608–1610.
checked: W. J. Griswold, The Great Anatolian Rebellion 1591–1611 (1983)

ev-ottoman-wahhabi-war:coord.reason: Plotted at Diriyah, besieged and destroyed by Ibrahim Pasha in 1818 (the war’s end); Wikidata 23,46 is an Arabia centroid. Route carries the Hejaz stops.
checked: M. Al-Rasheed, A History of Saudi Arabia (2010)
UNESCO World Heritage: At-Turaif District in ad-Dirʿiyah (https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1329/)

ev-mount-lebanon-1860:coord.reason: Plotted at Deir al-Qamar in Mount Lebanon, scene of one of the June 1860 massacres; Wikidata 34.30,36.12 lies in the northern Bekaa, away from the main violence. Note in record.
checked: L. T. Fawaz, An Occasion for War (1994)

ev-hamidian-massacres:coord.reason: Plotted at Sasun, where the massacres began in 1894; Wikidata 41,29 (Istanbul) marks only the 1896 killings in the capital.
checked: R. G. Suny, They Can Live in the Desert but Nowhere Else (2015)

ev-turkish-war-of-independence:year.reason: Wikidata’s 1922 is a point-in-time value (the Mudanya armistice); its own start is 19 May 1919, Kemal’s landing at Samsun, which this record uses.
checked: E. J. Zürcher, Turkey: A Modern History (2004)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Turkish War of Independence

ev-turkish-war-of-independence:coord.reason: Plotted at Ankara, seat of the Grand National Assembly from April 1920; Wikidata 39,35 is a centroid of Turkey. Route carries Samsun, Erzurum, Sivas, Sakarya, Dumlupınar, İzmir, Lausanne.
checked: E. J. Zürcher, Turkey: A Modern History (2004)

ev-iraqi-revolt-1920:coord.reason: Wikidata 33.83,35.83 is in Lebanon, clearly wrong. The revolt broke out at Rumaytha on the middle Euphrates (June 1920), where the record is plotted.
checked: C. Tripp, A History of Iraq (2007)

ev-1948-arab-israeli-war:coord.reason: Plotted at Latrun, on the fought-over road to Jerusalem (battles of May–July 1948); Wikidata 29.5,34 is in the southern Negev/Sinai. Note in record.

ev-six-day-war:coord.reason: Wikidata 28,45 lies in the Saudi desert. Plotted at Jerusalem, whose eastern part Israel took on 7 June 1967; the war had three fronts.
checked: M. B. Oren, Six Days of War (2002)

ev-uae-formed:coord.reason: Wikidata gives the UAE’s capital Abu Dhabi; the federation was proclaimed on 2 December 1971 at Union House (Al Ittihad), Dubai, where the record is plotted.
checked: F. Heard-Bey, From Trucial States to United Arab Emirates (2004)
Etihad Museum, Dubai (site of the signing)

ev-first-intifada:coord.reason: Plotted at Jabalia camp, Gaza, where the uprising began on 8–9 December 1987; Wikidata 32,35.35 is a generic West Bank point.
checked: R. Khalidi, The Hundred Years’ War on Palestine (2020)

ev-first-nagorno-karabakh-war:coord.reason: Plotted at Stepanakert (Khankendi), the region’s capital and focus of the conflict; Wikidata 40.3,47.7 is a lowland Azerbaijan point outside the mountain enclave.

ev-yemeni-civil-war:coord.reason: Plotted at Sanaa, whose seizure by the Houthis in September 2014 began the war; Wikidata 15.5,48 is a centroid of Yemen.

ev-gaza-war-2023:coord.reason: Wikidata 34,36 is in Lebanon. The war is centred on the Gaza Strip; plotted at Gaza City.

person-al-mutanabbi:born.reason: Britannica gives born 915, Kufa, died 23 Sept 965 near Dayr al-ʿAqul; the 1911 Britannica gives 915/6. Wikidata’s 920 has no better source.

person-hasan-i-sabbah:born.reason: Daftary in Encyclopaedia Iranica: born Qom in the mid-440s AH / 1050s, died Alamut 518/1124. Wikidata’s 1037 rests on no early source. Record medium with note.

person-osman-i:died.reason: Britannica: Osman died in 1324 or 1326; scholars place it in 1324, the year of Orhan’s first dated document, while tradition links it to the fall of Bursa (1326). Record low confidence, note gives both.

polity-first-saudi-state:from.reason: The Saudi state officially dates its founding to Muhammad ibn Saud’s accession at Diriyah on 22 Feb 1727 (royal decree, Jan 2022, Founding Day); Wikidata’s 1744 is the alliance with Ibn Abd al-Wahhab. Note gives both.
checked: Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Founding Day (https://mofa.gov.sa/en/ksa/Pages/foundingday.aspx)
M. Al-Rasheed, A History of Saudi Arabia (2010)

ev-battle-of-avarayr:coord.reason: 2026-11 review: the battle was fought on the Avarayr plain by the village of Churs (Chors) in West Azerbaijan, Iran (Wikidata Q5958318: 38.83, 45.035). Wikidata 39.34, 45.06 lies about 57 km further north, near Maku; it was copied from an infobox and does not match the plain the article itself names.

ev-ghaznavid-capture-of-rayy:year.reason: The QID is the wider Ghaznavid campaigns in Persia (1012–1034); this record is the capture of Rayy from Majd al-Dawla, dated March–May 1029 (Bosworth; Wikipedia: Majd al-Dawla). Note explains the proxy.

ev-ghaznavid-capture-of-rayy:coord.reason: Plotted at Rayy (Ray, south of modern Tehran), the city taken in 1029; Wikidata 30,52 is a generic point in Fars for the whole campaign series.
